text:
incident-bot: Paging S2 -> multiple GPU nodes in inference-prod are reporting driver resets (Xid 79/63) and a spike in OOMKills for inference-worker pods. 
incident-bot: Affected: node-42, node-47, node-58. ~22% of GPUs showing correctable ECC events in the last 10m. Auto-alert: perf-regression and pod restarts. 
oncall-amber: ack. Oncall here. Thanks for the alert. I'm grabbing the runbook: /runbooks/gpu-driver-reset.md :eyes: 
oncall-amber: first actions: cordon suspicious nodes, drain affected pods to fallback pool, open bridge if customers impacted. @infra-sam can you pull kernel logs and nv-host logs for node-42?
lee: on it. quick check: one pod shows OOMKilled and then crashlooped: 
```
$ kubectl describe pod inference-worker-7f4d -n inference
Status:  OOMKilled
Last State:  Terminated: OOMKilled
Containers:  worker
  State:  Waiting
  Reason: CrashLoopBackOff
  Last Termination:  Exit 137
Events:
  12m   Normal  Killing  Pod  Container needed to be killed for memory reclamation
```
maria: dmesg snippet from node-42 (relevant lines):
```
[ 1023.456789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=2431, GPU=a3 (0000:65:00.0)
[ 1023.457012] kernel: GPU memory ECC: single-bit corrected at addr 0x7f3bb1c000
[ 1023.457230] nvidia: GPU has corrected ECC errors, count=41
[ 1024.001112] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 63, pid=0, GPU=a3
```
lee: also seeing repeated nv-host reset entries in journalctl. nvidia-smi --query shows ResetCount incrementing.
infra-sam: I pulled nv-host logs + nvidia-smi output from node-42. ResetCount: 3 in the last 15m. Kernel messages show corrected ECC followed by gpu-reset. Suspect thermal/ECC burst or flaky PCI link.
infra-sam: Attempting graceful GPU reset on node-42 now (non-disruptive attempt). Command: `sudo nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i 0`
support-olivia: PS — CS reports 2 customers saw increased 5xxs and latency spikes on inference endpoints starting 10:14 UTC. We routed a small % to fallback model (redwood-small-quant) at 10:20 to reduce downstream errors. Notified account owners for those customers.
oncall-amber: ok, plan: 1) cordon node-42/47/58. 2) Drain pods to fallback pool. 3) If reset count>2 after reset, reboot node and collect full nv-host+kernel+hw telemetry. 4) If persists after reboot, escalate HW replacement.
lee: running drain now (going node by node): 
```
kubectl cordon node-42
kubectl drain node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=30
```
lee: note: using --delete-local-data because these inference pods have ephemeral local cache; we prefer to route traffic away quickly.
maria: pulled full dmesg and posted to ops logs: https://internal.logs/redwood/node-42/dmesg.txt. Also grabbed PCIe link stats: some link retrain events around Xid bursts.
infra-sam: after reset attempt, driver log still shows Xid 79 events. I'm going to collect hw telemetry and schedule a reboot in 5m. 
infra-sam: `systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced` first to clear dangling handles, if that doesn't help then reboot.
support-olivia: creating incident bridge for affected customers and CS comms: https://zoom.bridge/incident-3965201123 (bridge up). Adding affected customer list to incident doc. 
oncall-amber: thanks. @ops-bot can you throttle the deployment autoscaler for inference-prod to limit bursty scaling? We want to keep load predictable while we stabilize.
ops-bot: autoscaler: set targetBurstLimit=0 for inference-prod for 30m (temp). Rolling back after 30m unless overridden. :white_check_mark: 
lee: after draining node-42, pods came up in fallback pool but two pods still OOMKilled on node-47. Looks like memory pressure + transient GPU resets causing container restarts. Putting node-47 into maintenance (cordon + no-schedule).
maria: FYI for postmortem — these are correctable ECC events but frequency suggests either a failing DIMM / power transient or card-level issue. Reboots sometimes reduce resets for a while; repeated resets point to HW fault.
infra-sam: rebooting node-42 now, will attach serial logs and nv-host output to incident. If reboot clears resets, we still want to swap the GPU from that host out of rotation within 48h to be safe.
lee: live mitigation complete for now: traffic is at baseline, error rate down from 4.5% -> 0.6% after fallback routing. Keeping nodes cordoned until infra confirms stability.
support-olivia: notifying affected customers: CS outreach done, we offered temporary rate limit exemptions and ETA for follow-up.
oncall-amber: assigning postmortem: lee (owner), infra-sam (hardware investigation). Action items: collect kernel/nv-host logs, correlate PCIe events, check warranty swap if repeated after reboot, update runbook with explicit drain flags for inference workloads.
infra-sam: reimage / replace plan ready if resets reoccur after reboot. I also captured firmware versions and driver: NVIDIA 535.86, kernel 6.2. We should confirm if there's a matching driver advisory.
ops-bot: automated alert summary (metrics): 22% GPUs with ECC > threshold, 18 pods OOMKilled across 3 nodes, average latency spike +320ms for served requests. Link: https://metrics.internal/redwood/graph/incident-3965201123
oncall-amber: leaving handoff notes for night oncall. If anything flares back up, escalate to oncall-lead and open hardware replacement ticket. 
support-olivia: final note: bridge will stay open for 1h for followups. Will update customers after hardware investigation. :handshake: 
incident-bot: Incident S2 -> status: mitigated (fallback routing + node drain). Postmortem assigned.
